articles.title: Navicular fractures in elite athletes: Clarifying the evidence base of the 2025 International Foot and Ankle Sports Consensus.
articles.authors: Zimmermann FJ, Amling M, Simon A
articles.population: Elite athletes with navicular fractures
articles.outcomes: Return to sport timing after operative treatment of navicular stress fractures
articles.take_home: A previous systematic review reported return to sport at 8.2 weeks after surgery, but this appears to be a data extraction error. When recalculated correctly, the evidence suggests return to sport takes approximately 19.7 weeks (4.5 months) after surgery, which aligns with expert recommendations of 4 to 6 months.

articles.title: Quality and clinical implications of AI chatbot responses to common patient questions about total knee arthroplasty: a multidimensional comparative study.
articles.authors: Ekici M, Yalvac ES, Okur KT, Demir EB, Demir MA, Uner C, et al.
articles.population: AI chatbots accessed via free public interfaces
articles.sample_size: 9 chatbots evaluated on 5 common total knee arthroplasty patient questions, scored by 7 orthopaedic specialists
articles.outcomes: Quality, usability and transparency scores using QUEST, DISCERN, PEMAT-Understandability/Actionability, JAMA Benchmarks, Trust and Global Quality Score
articles.take_home: Different AI chatbots vary significantly in the quality, usability and trustworthiness of their answers about knee replacement surgery. Patients should be aware that not all AI chatbots provide equally reliable information for knee replacement questions.

articles.title: Mechanisms underlying the inhibition of chondrocyte apoptosis and inflammatory cytokine expression in knee osteoarthritis by rehmannia glutinosa polysaccharides via PI3K/AKT pathway activation at different concentrations.
articles.authors: Guo L, Xiao Z, Tan A
articles.study_type: Laboratory study using human knee osteoarthritis chondrocytes in vitro
articles.population: Human knee osteoarthritis chondrocytes
articles.outcomes: Cell viability, apoptosis markers (Caspase-3 activity, TUNEL staining), inflammatory cytokines (IL-1beta, IL-6, TNF-alpha), and PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activity
articles.take_home: In laboratory tests, rehmannia glutinosa polysaccharides improved cell survival and reduced inflammation in osteoarthritis cartilage cells by activating a specific cellular pathway. This effect was stronger at higher doses and could be blocked by a pathway inhibitor, suggesting the protective mechanism.

articles.title: Articular congruence, not neutrality: a systematic review of how native knee geometry shapes load-dependent alignment.
articles.authors: Ardiri D, Ciccolo G, Petrillo S
articles.population: Adult native knees from in-vivo imaging and cadaveric studies
articles.outcomes: Joint-line obliquity, frontal alignment, medio-lateral contact behaviour, contact area and pressure, meniscal extrusion, posterior tibial slope, tibial translation, antero-posterior contact behaviour
articles.take_home: The knee's shape naturally creates uneven contact surfaces that change how the joint tilts and moves depending on load and position, rather than staying in a fixed neutral alignment. This helps explain how healthy knees distribute weight and move dynamically.

articles.title: Two-year follow-up of postcommercialisation cohort of 100 bridge-enhanced anterior cruciate ligament restorations shows low retear rate and good patient-reported outcomes.
articles.authors: Wittstein J, Strickland S, Gomoll A, Sherman S, Lau B, Taylor D, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing bridge-enhanced anterior cruciate ligament restoration
articles.outcomes: Adverse events, reoperations, ACL retear rate, patient-reported outcomes (IKDC, KOOS, Marx, return to sport index) at 2 years
articles.take_home: The BEAR procedure showed a low ACL retear rate of 5.6% at 2 years, with improvements in patient-reported outcomes. A modified surgical technique reduced overall reoperation rates from 28% to 7.5% compared to the original technique.

articles.title: Outcomes of supramalleolar tibial derotational osteotomy in paediatric patients with recurrent patellar dislocation or anterior knee pain and associated torsional malalignment.
articles.authors: Dalal N, Denton M, Stanier P, Nicolaou N
articles.study_type: Observational study with prospective data collection
articles.population: Children with recurrent patellar dislocation or anterior knee pain and torsional malalignment of the tibia and femur
articles.sample_size: 30 knees in 21 patients, mean age 13.9 years
articles.outcomes: KOOS-Child score, Pedi-IKDC score, Kujala score, recurrent dislocation rates, need for further surgery
articles.take_home: Tibial derotation surgery in children with twisted leg bones and patellar dislocation or anterior knee pain significantly improved symptoms and function over 5 years, with no patients needing further surgery for recurrent dislocation. This approach may be more effective than stabilisation surgery alone for children with this specific type of leg misalignment.

articles.title: Acetabular morphology, centre-edge angle and cognitive impairment as predictors of dislocation and mortality after hip hemiarthroplasty.
articles.authors: Nehme Abouzeid F, Mardomingo Alonso A, Sanchez Gutierrez SJ, Galeote Lopez E, Rubio Quevedo R
articles.population: Patients treated with cemented bipolar hip hemiarthroplasty for intracapsular femoral neck fractures
articles.outcomes: Postoperative dislocation and mortality at 3 and 12 months
articles.take_home: Shallow hip sockets (acetabular depth less than 20 mm) and reduced centre-edge angles (less than 40 degrees) are strong predictors of hip dislocation after hemiarthroplasty surgery. Patients who dislocate have higher death rates, suggesting dislocation marks particularly frail patients who need closer monitoring.

articles.title: Range of motion simulated with patient-specific three-dimensional simulation analysis for evaluating anterior dislocation after total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Mitsutake R, Tanino H, Ito H
articles.study_type: Comparative cross-sectional study using three-dimensional simulation analysis
articles.population: Patients who had undergone total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Range of motion measurements including external rotation, extension angle, cup anteversion angle, and ischiofemoral length; identification of cutoff points associated with anterior dislocation risk
articles.take_home: Surgeons may be able to reduce the risk of hip dislocation after hip replacement by planning the operation to achieve greater range of motion and careful positioning of the hip socket during surgery. Specific measurements of joint movement and socket angle identified in this study could help guide preoperative planning.

articles.title: Global Projection of Revision Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty Through 2060: A 17-Country Analysis Using Worldwide Registry Data.
articles.authors: Adolf J, Karlidag T, Citak M
articles.study_type: Prognostic modelling study using registry data from 17 countries
articles.population: Adults aged 25 years and older in 17 countries with arthroplasty registries
articles.sample_size: 185,921 revision hip and 189,689 revision knee procedures in 2024 across the 17 countries
articles.outcomes: Projected annual volumes of revision total hip arthroplasty and revision total knee arthroplasty through 2060
articles.take_home: Revision hip and knee replacement surgery volumes across 17 major countries are projected to increase by about one-third by 2060, with the United States and China accounting for most growth whilst some European countries and Japan may see plateaus or declines.

articles.title: Early national comparison of robotic versus conventional knee replacements for arthritis using National Joint Registry data: target trial emulation study.
articles.authors: Mohammad HR, Judge A, Griffin XL, Murray DW
articles.study_type: Target trial emulation study using National Joint Registry data
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee replacement surgery in UK hospitals
articles.sample_size: 697,145 knee replacements (675,034 conventional, 22,111 robotic) between 2018 and 2024
articles.outcomes: Five year implant survival, revision risk, cause specific revision risk, intraoperative complications, and revision complexity comparing robotic versus conventional total knee replacement and unicompartmental knee replacement
articles.take_home: Robotic and conventional knee replacements showed similar survival rates and revision risks over five years, with no significant differences in safety or complications. The study suggests robotic surgery offers no clear advantage over conventional surgery despite its higher costs.

articles.title: Early national comparison of robotic versus conventional hip replacements for arthritis using National Joint Registry data: target trial emulation study.
articles.authors: Mohammad HR, Judge A, Griffin XL, Murray DW
articles.study_type: Target trial emulation study using national registry data
articles.population: People having total hip replacement for arthritis in UK hospitals
articles.outcomes: Five-year implant survival, revision rates, complications, patient survival, and risk of revisions due to implant malposition
articles.take_home: Robotic and conventional hip replacements had similar survival rates and overall safety, but robotic surgery had a lower risk of revisions due to implant malposition. However, robotic surgery costs considerably more, so the small advantage needs careful evaluation in the NHS.

articles.title: Detection of previous knee injuries using lower limb-worn inertial measurement units: A cross-sectional machine-learning study.
articles.authors: Valle C, Cotic M, Bartelt M, Seeberger L, Waschulzik B, Siebenlist S, et al.
articles.population: Physically active sports science students
articles.sample_size: 90 participants (23 with previous knee injury, 67 uninjured controls)
articles.outcomes: Machine learning model ability to detect previous knee injury using wearable motion sensors, with sensitivity 48%, specificity 97%, and area under receiver operating characteristic curve 0.74
articles.take_home: Wearable motion sensors worn on the legs could potentially detect signs of previous knee injury in physically active people, though the test was better at identifying those without previous injury (97% specificity) than those with it (48% sensitivity). More research is needed to confirm these findings work reliably in different groups of people.

articles.title: Improved function and patient satisfaction with fewer residual symptoms following kinematically versus mechanically aligned total knee arthroplasty: A retrospective study from FP-UCBM Knee Study Group.
articles.authors: Campi S, Giurazza G, Franceschetti E, Hirschmann MT, Tanzilli A, Paciotti M, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee replacement for end-stage osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Patient satisfaction, functional performance, residual symptoms, joint awareness measured using Forgotten Joint Score and Joint Awareness Score
articles.take_home: Patients who received kinematically aligned knee replacements reported higher satisfaction (94% versus 81%), better function such as easier getting in and out of chairs, and fewer symptoms like pain and popping compared to those receiving mechanically aligned replacements at one year follow-up.

articles.title: Short- to mid-term outcomes of total hip arthroplasty in high hip dislocations: does age matter?
articles.authors: Basaran SH, Imre E, Yalin M, Bayrak A, Donmez B, Demircan E
articles.population: Patients with Crowe 3-4 high hip dislocations undergoing cementless total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 77 patients (43 aged under 60 years, 34 aged 60 years or older)
articles.outcomes: Harris Hip Score, SF-36 scores, complications including deep vein thrombosis, and revision-free survival at 2 and 3 years
articles.take_home: Age alone does not affect long-term outcomes or functional improvement after hip replacement in patients with high hip dislocations. Older patients had more complications, but this was linked to existing health conditions rather than age itself, and good surgical care can achieve similar results regardless of age.

articles.title: Functional outcomes after total hip arthroplasty in young patients: comparison of patients younger than 35 years versus patients aged 35-40 years.
articles.authors: Krautter J, Deckert M, Feil S, Thorey F
articles.population: Young patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty, aged under 40 years
articles.sample_size: 68 hips in 54 participants (35 patients aged under 35 years, 33 patients aged 35-40 years)
articles.outcomes: Hip disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score (HOOS), Harris Hip Score (HHS), visual analogue scale (VAS) pain score, and Oxford Hip Score (OHS)
articles.take_home: Total hip replacement in young patients under 40 years improved pain, function and quality of life significantly, with both age groups showing similar good outcomes and high patient satisfaction. Very few complications occurred, with less than 3% requiring revision surgery.

articles.title: Risk Factors for 30- and 1-year mortality in the Australian Hip Fracture Cohort: insights from the Australian and New Zealand Hip Fracture Registry.
articles.authors: Marasco S, Wong Z, Cheok T, Wall C, Hau R
articles.population: Older adults with hip fractures in Australia and New Zealand
articles.outcomes: 30-day mortality and 1-year mortality, with identification of associated risk factors
articles.take_home: Having surgery sooner after a hip fracture significantly reduces the risk of death within 30 days and one year. Delays of more than 48 hours due to medical problems or other reasons substantially increase the risk of dying in the year after fracture.

articles.title: Aseptic loosening of small hydroxyapatite-coated quadrangular tapered femoral stems: camouflage in the Canadian Joint Replacement Registry.
articles.authors: Righolt CH, Poitras C, Bansal R, Burnell CD, Turgeon TR, Bohm ER
articles.study_type: Observational cohort study using registry data
articles.population: Patients who had primary total hip replacement surgery between 2012 and 2023
articles.sample_size: 21,843 hip replacements (1,547 Avenir, 16,893 Corail, 3,403 Polarstem stems)
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery for aseptic loosening (the artificial joint coming loose without infection)
articles.take_home: Very small femoral stems (the implant that goes in the thigh bone) have a much higher risk of needing revision surgery, particularly when paired with larger hip sockets. Surgeons should be cautious about using smaller stems than preoperative planning suggests, as this mismatch significantly increases the risk of the implant loosening.

articles.title: Retatrutide in adults with obesity and type 2 diabetes (TRIUMPH-2): a double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial.
articles.authors: Bellido V, le Roux CW, Ekinci EI, Bjornstad P, Frias JP, Giblin K, et al.
articles.study_type: Double-blind, parallel-group, randomised, placebo-controlled phase 3 trial
articles.population: Adults aged 18 years and over with obesity (BMI 27 kg/m² or higher) and type 2 diabetes on stable treatment
articles.sample_size: 1152 participants randomly assigned (4 mg: 292, 9 mg: 284, 12 mg: 287, placebo: 289)
articles.outcomes: Percentage change in bodyweight at week 80; glycaemic control (HbA1c); gastrointestinal adverse events (diarrhoea, nausea), hypotension, and dysesthesia; treatment discontinuation due to adverse events
articles.take_home: Retatrutide reduced weight by 12 to 19 percent depending on dose, compared with 5 percent for placebo, and improved blood sugar control in people with obesity and type 2 diabetes. The most common side effects were diarrhoea and nausea, which occurred more frequently at higher doses.

articles.title: Retatrutide, a Triple Hormone Receptor Agonist, for Treatment of Obesity.
articles.authors: Jastreboff AM, Kaplan LM, Davies MJ, Wilding JPH, Ahmad NN, Murray M, et al.
articles.population: Adults with obesity without diabetes
articles.sample_size: 2339 participants (574 with knee osteoarthritis, 243 with obstructive sleep apnea)
articles.outcomes: Percentage change in body weight, WOMAC pain score in knee osteoarthritis, apnea-hypopnea index in obstructive sleep apnea
articles.take_home: Retatrutide, given as a weekly injection, led to significant weight loss (23.7-25.0% with higher doses versus 3.9% with placebo) and also reduced knee pain and sleep apnea events in people with these conditions. The most common side effects were gastrointestinal problems.

articles.title: Do Not Chase Symmetric Gaps: Native Asymmetry Linked to Better Recovery in Fixed-Deformity Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Suhardi VJ, Gwam C, DiGangi C, Hepinstall M, Rozell J, Meftah M
articles.study_type: Retrospective comparative analysis of robotic-arm-assisted total knee replacements
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty, stratified by whether their knee deformity could be corrected
articles.sample_size: 861 patients (634 with correctable deformity, 227 with non-correctable fixed deformity)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported functional outcomes at one year measured by Knee injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (KOOS JR) and PROMIS Physical Function; relationship between bone resection volume, gap symmetry, and recovery
articles.take_home: In patients with fixed knee deformities that cannot be fully straightened, keeping the knee's natural side-to-side looseness rather than removing extra bone to create perfectly balanced gaps leads to better recovery and function at one year. This suggests surgeons should preserve the patient's own anatomy rather than forcing symmetry in these difficult cases.

articles.title: Preoperative Contralateral Joint And/Or Back Pain Impact on Achieving the Substantial Clinical Benefit for Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score-Joint Replacement.
articles.authors: Elmenawi KA, Jevnikar BE, Oyem PC, Jin Y, Krebs VE, Molloy RM, et al.
articles.population: Medicare patients undergoing primary total hip replacement
articles.outcomes: Achievement of substantial clinical benefit (22-point improvement in Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score-Joint Replacement), minimal clinically important difference, patient-acceptable symptom state, and satisfaction at one year
articles.take_home: Patients with back pain and/or pain in the other hip before surgery were significantly less likely to achieve good outcomes after hip replacement, with those having both types of pain being over three times more likely to not reach the clinical benefit target. Pain severity mattered too, with severe back pain more than doubling the risk of poor outcomes.

articles.title: Practice Management Strategies Among the Current Members of the American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons.
articles.authors: Lieberman JR, Buller LT, Meneghini RM
articles.population: American Association of Hip and Knee Surgeons members
articles.outcomes: Practice setting, compensation method, and adoption of outpatient total joint arthroplasty
articles.take_home: Most hip and knee surgeons still work in private practice, but hospital employment is growing. The way surgeons are paid is shifting from fee for service towards relative value units, and same-day discharge after joint replacement surgery is now standard.
